name: Sprout Money Market Fund
description: Very short-term, high-quality loans to governments and banks. Built to hold steady; earns roughly the cash rate.

name: Treasury Bill Fund
description: US government loans of under a year. Moves very little; a home for money you need soon.

name: Short-Term Treasury Fund
description: US government bonds that mature in about 2 years. Small ups and downs, a little more income than cash.

name: Treasury Bond Index Fund
description: US government bonds around 10 years. Pays steady interest; prices fall when interest rates rise.

name: Government Bond Ladder Fund
description: A ladder of US government bonds near 10 years, held to spread out when bonds mature.

name: US Total Market Index Fund
description: Thousands of US companies of every size. Can drop a lot in a bad year; has grown over long periods.

name: US Large Company Index Fund
description: The largest US companies. Similar ups and downs to the whole US market.

name: Developed Markets ex-US Index Fund
description: Large companies in Europe, Japan, Canada and Australia. Spreads risk beyond the US.

name: International Equity Index Fund
description: A second broad fund for developed markets outside the US.

name: Emerging Markets Index Fund
description: Companies in fast-growing economies such as China, India and Brazil. Bigger swings than developed markets.

name: Gold Fund
description: Tracks the price of gold. Often moves differently from stocks, but can fall for years.

name: Global Technology Fund
description: Technology companies only. One sector, so it can rise or fall much more than the whole market.

name: Star Manager Growth Fund
description: A fund where a manager picks US stocks. Charges much higher fees than an index fund.
